_note: INFORMATION TEXTS for the English literacy year (Daily Teaching System, Part 12.3; read by a US Grade 1 reading reviewer 2026-11-15 and corrected by every finding; read a second time after the corrections (four small wording points, applied)). The reading banks held stories only; the Common Core RI standards need texts that inform. Grade 1: about 60 to 75 words in two sections, each with a heading; two words in bold; a three-word glossary; one library picture with a caption. Every fact must be one a teacher can confirm; every question has one right answer that a sentence of the text gives (its 1-based number is `sentence`). `topic` = the main topic and two wrong choices (a detail of the text; a thing the text only mentions). `full` = the whole answer sentence of a question (it starts with `starter`); `lure` = a word of the text that is not in bold (a wrong choice of the bold-word question); `capChoices` = two wrong answers of the caption question; `picture2` = a second picture of something the text tells about, with a sample caption. `features` = find-it questions answered from a text feature, not from the running text. `headLure` = a heading the text does not have (the third choice of a heading question: a child may call the title the main heading). KINDERGARTEN (`k`, DRAFT 2026-11-15, read by no reviewer, used by no page): four sentences in big print; every question is read aloud by the teacher and answered by circling one of three library pictures (`right`, `wrong`); `topic` = the picture of the main topic and two pictures of details; `details` = the numbers of the two sentences that are key details.
